stances.claim: Under UNCLOS and the AA, the Philippines holds sovereign rights -- not sovereignty -- over the marine resources within its EEZ, including those at Whitsun (a Low-Tide Elevation), which falls inside the PH EEZ at 175 NM from Bataraza.

If China can prove sovereignty over Hughes/McKennan as High-Tide Elevations AND that Whitsun lies within their 12-NM territorial seas, then under the AA itself China would be entitled to the resources at Whitsun -- a question of fact for the ICJ, not the PCA.
stances.rhetorical_move: conditional-concession framing (if-repeat-if) anchored to the very AA Manila invokes

stances.claim: PD 1596 cannot prevail over UNCLOS and the AA, because it was issued before the Philippines signed UNCLOS in 1982 and is deemed modified by both -- and Manila's victorious invocation of the AA over its EEZ estops it from denying the AA's unfavorable parts.

China will not actually invoke the AA because doing so would concede the AA's authority -- which would in turn negate its rejected nine-dash line claim; this internal contradiction is China's binding limit, not the Philippines'.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-trap diagnosis (China is structurally barred from using the very instrument it would need)
stances.confidence: asserted with confidence ('I doubt that China will do that')

stances.claim: A united, simultaneous recourse under the rule of law to the ICJ is the best path -- diplomacy alone is fine but insufficient; the ICJ is the proper venue China itself recognizes for land-feature sovereignty disputes.

notable_anecdotes: The Torrens-title-vs-lease metaphor -- sovereign rights over EEZ resources are likened to enjoying trees, plants, and fruits on a leased adjoining parcel, but not the Torrens title to the land -- translating UNCLOS distinctions into Philippine real-property idiom.

The 'if--repeat, if--' conditional rhetorical device used to telegraph that CJ is granting a hypothetical without conceding the fact, then converting the conditional into a recommendation that China itself put the question to the ICJ.

The estoppel hinge -- Manila's 'victorious use of the AA to justify our sovereign rights over our huge EEZ estops us from denying its unfavorable parts' -- turning legal-consistency into the moral-high-ground argument.

The Filipino-style enumeration of the six Spratly HTEs (Scarborough, Gaven North, McKennan, Johnson, Cuarteron, Fiery Cross) directly from the AA's dispositive paragraph 1203-B-3-b -- used to anchor the column in primary text rather than commentary.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban clarifies the legal status of Julian Felipe Reef (English: Whitsun; Chinese: Niu'e Jiao) under UNCLOS, the July 12, 2016 Arbitral Award, and Philippine domestic law. Coastal states are granted sovereign rights -- not sovereignty -- over the marine resources within a 200-NM Exclusive Economic Zone, akin to a lease's right to fruits without Torrens title to the land. Whitsun, a Low-Tide Elevation lying 175 NM west of Bataraza, Palawan, sits within the PH EEZ. However, Whitsun is alleged to be within the 12-NM territorial sea of McKennan Reef, judged a High-Tide Elevation by AA Paragraph 1203-B-3-b -- and under UNCLOS the TS of an HTE is an enclave superior to the overlapping EEZ. China asserts sovereignty over McKennan, Hughes, and most of the South China Sea under its nine-dash line (rejected by the AA), justifying its swarm of vessels and fishing ban; Vietnam asserts sovereignty over Sin Cowe Island (judged an HTE by Paragraph 1203-B-3-f) and claims Whitsun lies within its TS. Manila's claim rests on Marcos's 1978 PD 1596 declaring the Kalayaan Island Group part of Philippine territory -- but the PD predates Manila's 1982 UNCLOS signing and is deemed modified by UNCLOS and the AA, and Manila's victorious use of the AA for the EEZ estops it from denying unfavorable parts. CJ predicts China will not actually invoke the AA because doing so would concede the very authority that overturned its nine-dash claim. The right path, in his humble opinion, is a clear, united, and simultaneous recourse under the rule of law to the ICJ -- the body whose decisions are international law and are invariably implemented by the United Nations.
